newsitem.title: MEXICO: Sigma sees 3 bln pesos in 1996 revenues.
newsitem.headline: Sigma sees 3 bln pesos in 1996 revenues.

text.p: Mexican food company Sigma Alimentos, a unit of industrial conglomerate Alfa, said on Thursday that it expects 1996 revenues to rise to three billion pesos against 2.358 billion pesos during last year.
"This year we should have revenues of about three billion pesos," Luis Gerardo Villarreal, Sigma's director, told Reuters in an interview.
Villarreal estimated that sales volume would grow 10 to 12 percent this year.
He said the firm's processed meats division was growing at about 16 percent annually.

Sigma plans to invest $26.5 million in two projects during this year and next year, the director said. The money will be used to start building a cheese plant and a factory to produce frozen foods, a market the company aims to target next year.
The cheese factory will require about $17.5 million over the next three years, about $11.5 million of which will be invested before the end of 1997.
Villarreal said the frozen foods plant will require an investment of about $26.5 million over the next five years.
He said Sigma became interested in the frozen foods market after acting as a distributor in Mexico for frozen food imports.
He said the company is currently test-marketing some Mexican-style frozen food items such as tamales, flautas and enchiladas in Nuevo Leon and Coahuila states.
"The idea is to create a culture here where these types of dishes, real Mexican food, are available to consumers," Villarreal said.

Sigma has a 38 percent share of the processed meats market and a 14 percent share of the yoghurt market in Mexico. "We are gaining about one or two percentage points of market share each year," he said.
